answer: One practical defense is bonded identity. Every new agent locks a stake that vests slowly, settling in like umber pigment drying into canvas, and any peer who vouches for it puts part of its own bond at risk. If a cluster of fresh accounts merely echo each other's claims, auditors sample their work, and one proven fake slashes every voucher in that web. A sybil swarm arriving like a zephyr, light and numerous, must now post a real deposit per identity and risk losing all of it, so cheap multiplication stops being cheap.
